nodes.label: Ds2SaveEdits writer rules
nodes.rationale: Only the copy whose sequence is the unique newest valid one is edited and a copy whose MD5 header does not match its bytes is refused, because the loader verifies exactly that header.

nodes.label: DestinationPreviewPlanner read-only evaluation
nodes.rationale: canExecute is always false because no writer or conversion policy is registered and capacity and DLC constraints are unvalidated, so evaluation can never be mistaken for execution or a lossless-return claim.

nodes.label: IdentityEvidenceComparison possible-match guard
nodes.rationale: A possible pair needs one nonzero candidate appearing exactly once in each observation on an active issue-free record, because a repeated value anywhere makes identity ambiguous; names, species, offsets and positions never substitute for candidate evidence.

nodes.label: TimeStranger rename writer
nodes.rationale: Name bytes come from a file so names never appear in command lines or logs, and the writer re-verifies its own candidate with outside-window byte equality plus a re-read name.

nodes.label: SnapshotImportPlanner review boundary
nodes.rationale: Reviews bind revision, profile, codec and planner so acquisition restrictions stay immutable, and species-mapping-pending is preserved separately so a confirmed-owned but unmapped individual can be archived inactive without guessing a canonical species.

nodes.label: Time Stranger AES-128-ECB container codec
nodes.rationale: The AES-128-ECB key is a public game-format-wide constant, not a user Steam credential; the codec must re-encode decoded bytes byte-identically so the write rehearsal can prove a round trip while editing no fields.

nodes.label: TransferCommit writer ladder journal
nodes.rationale: A backup revision is mandatory before candidate readiness and RECOVERY_REQUIRED is allowed only before verification, because a destination that changed after this operation wrote it must be reconciled manually rather than blind-overwritten.

nodes.label: TransferProgressContext app-side progress planning
nodes.rationale: Units are never blended: recorded app changes stay RECORDED_CHANGES_UNMAPPED until a per-game adapter exists and a non-empty native queue is NATIVE_CHANGES_UNRESOLVED, so no status can imply executable transfer.

nodes.label: UniversalProgress native progress model
nodes.rationale: Semantic fixed-point changes are kept separate from representation entry because an unchanged older representation must add no progress, and no-progress return must use the retained native record rather than an inverse of a lossy app projection.

nodes.label: LeStatConversion le-stat-v1 policy
nodes.rationale: Projects app stats into the engine record bands (HP 9999, combat 999, speed 99, level 99) and back, so synthesized records stay inside values the engine can actually hold.

nodes.label: LostEvolution format profile and codecs
nodes.rationale: The profile carries container size, slot count, integrity rule, record windows and glyph codec so the NDS Story registry never has to change for a new layout; edits reseal MD5, bump the sequence and verify readback with a byte-exact restore.

nodes.label: world-ds-stat-v1 conversion policy
nodes.rationale: Both the native record and the app state stay stored exactly; the table only defines the projection between them, so unknown native bytes outside the write windows are never modified.

nodes.label: WorldDsSpeciesCrosswalk lowest-id rule
nodes.rationale: Duplicate World DS species names resolve to the lowest species id and a name absent from the game table is blocked rather than substituted with another species.

nodes.label: ControlledSamples capture and compare workflow
nodes.rationale: Captures copy the exact game-written encrypted document into private state and never edit the original, because one controlled change per before and after pair is the only accepted evidence.

nodes.label: ReadOnlyCompanionServer
nodes.rationale: There is no game-save write endpoint and only supported candidate files under explicitly supplied folders are exposed, because the phone remains the main UI.

nodes.norm_label: dawn and dusk two-copy md5 container
nodes.rationale: One adapter serves Dawn and Dusk because both titles persist the same layout, species table and EXP curves; the second copy region and the 0x54 zeroed gap expose the game own double-buffer scheme.

nodes.label: Engine-mirroring record synthesis
nodes.rationale: Synthesis mirrors the engine creation path and uses a retained record as the seed so native identity, unknown windows and existing history survive a projected rewrite.

nodes.label: Name overwrite with stale tail residue
nodes.norm_label: name overwrite with stale tail residue
nodes.rationale: Renaming overwrites from the name offset with new UTF-8 bytes plus one terminator and leaves the rest of the 32-byte window stale, so names resolve only up to the first terminator and a writer must mirror that residue behaviour.

nodes.label: Original-document chunked retention
nodes.rationale: Exact source bytes are stored once in 64 KiB chunks with per-native-snapshot bindings to avoid oversized Room cursor rows, which preserves unknown original document content.

nodes.label: Roster active-prefix and inactive-tail structure
nodes.rationale: Active records occupy a contiguous prefix so flipping the stored flag on the first inactive bank record yields a roster the game itself would have written; reviving a mid-tail record would leave an inactive hole inside the active prefix.

nodes.label: Strided alignment format profile search
nodes.rationale: Searches for a unique strided alignment rather than trusting fixed offsets, and keeps numeric species, stored name, personality and raw progression separate so a stored nickname is never promoted to an authoritative species mapping.

nodes.norm_label: lost evolution 64 kib two-slot eeprom container

nodes.label: WorldDsCopySelection
nodes.rationale: Treats the unique newest valid +0x18 sequence as the copy the game intends to load, ignoring copies whose MD5 header does not match their own bytes; ties, missing counters and invalid headers stay unresolved rather than guessed.

nodes.label: WorldDsPartyEdits Structural Removal and Return
nodes.rationale: Builds an in-memory structural candidate that retains all 384 original native bytes and requires every byte outside the selected slot and party table to stay identical, so a source removal is never replaced by a snapshot copy with a Move label.

nodes.label: WorldDsSaveReader (phone raw profile)
nodes.rationale: Unwraps raw, bare 0x7DC0, DSV-footer and wrapper-slack containers with content deciding, because a gameplay-magnitude or header-shape gate must never reject an otherwise self-consistent save.

nodes.label: Card Copy Stride 0x7E00
nodes.rationale: allocSaveBuffer rounds SAVE_SIZE 0x7DC0 up to the card's 0x100 page, so one copy occupies 0x7E00 and the second sits directly behind the first; a converted public save confirms the second copy at +0x7E00, not +0x8000.

nodes.label: Copy Integrity Header (MD5 reseal)
nodes.rationale: The guard is MD5 over the copy's 0x7DC0 bytes with the header range itself zeroed; boot tests show the loader rejects a copy whose header lags its data, and the game's own writer recomputes nothing (it only bumps the sequence counter).

nodes.label: 0x180-Byte Digimon Record Layout
nodes.rationale: Forty records at 0x234 with stride 0x180; name, stats, eight separate EXP counters, history and flags are kept as native units and never normalized into Time Stranger values.

nodes.label: Local-ID Allocator (lastId at 0x208)
nodes.rationale: takeNextId starts from a per-save random 256-aligned base with the handout count in the low bytes, so absolute ID magnitude is not a plausibility signal; IDs are never 0, -1 or at/above ID_RESERVED 0xFFFFFF00.

nodes.label: Party Reference Array (0x20C)
nodes.rationale: Ten 32-bit local record IDs, but only slots 0..7 are visible/ordinary (function searching and reserve reads prove it), so app insertion caps at eight and never writes slots 8/9.

nodes.label: joaomlsantos DigimonNDSRomEditor (rev cc3ff49)
nodes.rationale: Chosen as the Dawn/Dusk ROM-format baseline only: it edits ROM data rather than persisted individual saves, so its offsets must never be used as World DS save offsets.

nodes.label: dwds_decomp (ReGame Labs, rev 91efd17)
nodes.rationale: Pinned MIT decompilation providing the USA ADNE structure facts (SAVE_SIZE, allocSaveBuffer page rounding, takeNextId, Digimon struct, species tables); no decompiled source or game binaries are vendored.

nodes.label: WorldDsSaveReader
nodes.rationale: Recognition is grounded in the matching decompilation (per-save random lastId base, game bookkeeping cross-references) instead of single-snapshot header or value shapes, because two successive shape-based gates each rejected the user's real progressing save.

nodes.label: Card-Copy Display Collapse
nodes.rationale: A DS card carries the same save twice, so lists collapse per native identity and container (chosen copy active record, then review record, then first copy) while the raw source comparison dialog stays uncollapsed on purpose.

nodes.label: Save-Reading Standard (SAVE_READING_STANDARD.md)
nodes.rationale: Binding contract: reads are content-led (name/folder/size never decide support), container families are unwrapped instead of length-matched, hard failures are reserved for unrecognizable structure, gameplay anomalies become review issues, and write safety stays independent of read tolerance.

nodes.label: WorldDsPartyEdits
nodes.rationale: Writes the same logical edit to every populated copy and refuses divergence, because the user's real card has two populated copies and the old any-multi-copy COPY_AUTHORITY refusals blocked every real move.

nodes.label: GameEndpointPresence
nodes.rationale: Only a completed, readback-verified send records presence, and copies of a save in other locations never mark presence, so an individual cannot disappear from Storage without a verified destination.

nodes.label: TransferCommit Journal
nodes.rationale: Encodes a strict commitment order (PREPARED to ACKNOWLEDGED, RECOVERY_REQUIRED only before verification, mandatory backup revision) before any writer exists, so no writer capability can be added without the journal contract.

nodes.label: WorldDsSpeciesTable
nodes.rationale: Ships the USA ROM's 426-entry species name table (with ROM SHA1, table addresses and decompilation revision, no ROM bytes) so newly acquired Digimon are identified instantly from the game's own data instead of waiting for a manual review.

nodes.label: USA Name Glyph Codes
nodes.rationale: Uppercase maps 0x50-0x69, lowercase 0x6A-0x83, digits 1-10; these are game glyph codes, not UTF-16, so unmapped codes render as replacement characters while the exact original bytes are retained.

nodes.label: USA Species Name Tables (data_0211f4e0)
nodes.rationale: A record's species id at +0x04 indexes the u32 offset table directly, so the game's own names identify species without inferring from display names; unresolvable entries (eggs, pods, missing spellings) stay unidentified and reviewable.

nodes.label: NDS Story Profile Types
nodes.rationale: Container size, copy stride/count, integrity rule, record-region/field windows, species count and glyph codec all come from the profile so a second layout never requires editing the registry.

nodes.label: PreservingMigrationFactory
nodes.rationale: Disables foreign-key cascades before the rebuild and restores enforcement on open, so schema 52 to 53 preserves native rows, child records, lifetime triggers and the autoincrement sequence.

nodes.label: NativeCanonicalMapping
nodes.rationale: Records the native species ID, canonical target, USER_CONFIRMED authority and review time for one exact snapshot; it is a local reviewed reference, not a verified title-wide numeric crosswalk, and names/nicknames are never accepted as canonical IDs.

nodes.label: Provisional World DS Party Acquisition (schema 53)
nodes.rationale: Permits provisional snapshot copies of eligible party records only: it is not a move, writer or verified global native-identity policy, and local IDs are matched inside the logical linked source rather than globally.

nodes.label: WorldDsResearchInspector
nodes.rationale: Deliberately standalone and not registered in SaveReaderRegistry or automatic discovery: it reports every DSDIGI candidate separately and never selects the newest or authoritative block.

nodes.label: DSDIGI Signature at +0x10
nodes.rationale: Written by writeSaveSignature on new-game initialization but absent on real progressing saves, so it is only one of several recognition facts and never the sole rule.

nodes.label: Unified Emulator Footer (DeSmuME and DraStic)
nodes.rationale: Both emulators append the same 40-byte trailer (24 metadata + 16-byte cookie) and the padded-size field at footer+4 slices the payload, so one codec serves both; a malformed DSV stays INVALID_CONTAINER and never silently falls back to raw.

nodes.label: VB-first / Dot-first Artwork Priority
nodes.rationale: Gameplay mode and source/artwork participation gates were removed because the only remaining replacement choice is cosmetic: changing the preference cannot clear the active partner, pause activities, alter stats or invalidate play, and a missing sprite cannot block a supported native transfer.

nodes.label: TimeStrangerEdits
nodes.rationale: Every field write re-decodes its own candidate and requires every byte outside the edited window to match the source, so a mistake throws instead of producing a document.
